chunks: And in it, he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to the servants in the distribution of the khums.
But He places in it something by which He tests His servants.
ai.seo_question: Why is the distribution of khums considered a test for believers?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records the Imam explaining that the division of khums serves as a divine test of obedience and gratitude, rather than an arbitrary act of God. This perspective aligns with the Shia theological view that financial obligations are mechanisms for spiritual purification and social justice, reinforcing the believer's reliance on divine wisdom.
